title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is witnessing a flurry of activity as companies seek to solidify their positions amidst growing competition and funding opportunities. Notably, acquisitions and strategic partnerships are shaping the landscape, while concerns about hardware durability in low Earth orbit loom large.

themes.title: Acquisitions and Partnerships
themes.body: MDA Space's acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies signals a strategic move to bolster its presence in the U.S. market. Meanwhile, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical satellite constellation bid, highlighting the trend of collaboration in a fragmented industry.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy
themes.body: ElevationSpace's recent $40 million Series B funding round underscores the increasing investor appetite for space startups. With True Anomaly also raising $190 million, it seems that venture capital is still keen on backing the next big thing in space.

themes.title: Production and Resilience
themes.body: Northrop Grumman's confidence in scaling solid rocket production reflects a broader industry readiness to meet demand. Coupled with a $1.4 billion budget increase for space resilience, it appears that the U.S. is doubling down on its space capabilities.

themes.title: Durability Concerns
themes.body: The ongoing MEO durability crisis raises alarms about the longevity of LEO hardware in the emerging orbital economy. As companies push for more ambitious missions, the question remains: can current technologies withstand the test of time?
